title: Modus Tollens
body:
**Modus tollens** takes a [[Material Conditional]] and the negation of its consequent to
the negation of its antecedent.

```
P → Q
¬Q
-----
¬P
```

```
If the program compiled, there are no syntax errors.
There is a syntax error.
So the program did not compile.
```

It is the contrapositive used as a rule, since `P→Q` and `¬Q→¬P` are equivalent, and it is how
a hypothesis is refuted by testing a prediction it makes: derive a consequence, show the
consequence is false, and the hypothesis falls.

The invalid pattern that resembles it is denying the antecedent, taking `P→Q` and `¬P` to `¬Q`.
That fails because the conditional says nothing about what happens when `P` is false.
